Because the breakeven point represents the normal profit situation where the average revenue (AR) of the firm is equal to the average cost (AC). A firm will continue to produce below the breakeven point as long as it is earning average revenue (AR) greater than minimum average variable cost (AVC). The minimum average variable cost is called the shutdown point, after which production will be stopped.
